answer: Inter-arrival variance gating. Each agent identity must show human-plausible gaps between its actions, like a quill drawn at irregular speed: the system scores variance in inter-action timing over a rolling window. Synthetic fleets emit near-constant cadence, so they fail the variance floor and get rate-limited. An attacker must insert randomized delays and idle periods per identity, renting or scripting slow traffic across every alias—costing wall-clock time and scheduler overhead that scales linearly with fleet size. A single ember of activity cannot mask a river of clones.
